stem:
A 45-year-old man with bone marrow failure has a platelet count far below normal. His marrow biopsy shows a marked reduction in large cells with lobed nuclei measuring 50-100 micrometers.

Platelets are produced by fragmentation of which of the following cells?

options.label: A
options.misconception: An immature red cell is being treated as the platelet source.
options.explanation: Reticulocytes are immature erythrocytes that mature into red blood cells; platelets bud off megakaryocyte cytoplasm instead.

options.label: B
options.misconception: The macrophage precursor is being confused with the platelet precursor.
options.explanation: Monocytes differentiate into macrophages and dendritic cells in tissues; they do not fragment into platelets.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; platelets are megakaryocyte cytoplasmic fragments.
options.explanation: A platelet is not a cell but a fragment of the cytoplasm of a megakaryocyte surrounded by plasma membrane; each megakaryocyte releases 2,000-3,000 platelets, and thrombopoietin from the kidneys and liver stimulates their production.

options.label: D
options.misconception: An antibody-secreting cell is being cast as a platelet source.
options.explanation: Plasma cells are differentiated B lymphocytes that secrete antibodies; platelets arise only from megakaryocyte cytoplasm.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Vessel-lining cells are being treated as a formed-element source.
options.explanation: Endothelial cells line blood vessels and contribute von Willebrand factor, but platelets are fragments of marrow megakaryocytes.

context: Learning objective: derive platelets. Platelets are membrane-bound cytoplasmic fragments of megakaryocytes — large (50-100 micrometer) marrow cells with lobed nuclei — released in thousands per cell. Thrombopoietin, secreted by the kidneys and liver, stimulates megakaryoblast proliferation.
